turns.content: An integer-valued function f on the positive integers is called tenuous when f(x)+f(y)>x^2 for every ordered pair x,y. Apply the condition in both orders and use integrality to derive a symmetric lower bound for f(x)+f(y).
Apply that bound to the ten complementary pairs (1,20),(2,19),...,(10,11). What lower bound does each pair contribute, and why is this pairing useful for the sum of the first twenty values?
Add the ten paired inequalities to obtain a numerical lower bound for f(1)+f(2)+...+f(20).

Show that the bound is attainable by considering g(n)=61 for n<=10 and g(n)=n^2-60 for n>=11. Verify the tenuous condition for every possible placement of x and y relative to 10, and compute the first-twenty sum.

Now let g be any tenuous function whose first-twenty sum attains that minimum. Show that every complementary-pair inequality must be an equality, then prove that g(1)=...=g(10)=a and determine g(n) for 11<=n<=20 in terms of a.
Use the self-pair x=y=11 to bound a, and deduce the least value that g(14) can have among all minimizing tenuous functions.
Check that equality is genuinely possible at that value of a: reconcile the paired equalities with the all-positive-integers construction and verify the resulting value of g(14).
State the minimum possible value of g(14), together with the two facts that make the bound sharp.
